explain: A missing acknowledgment leaves the client uncertain even after the server committed. Reconnect should query or reuse the same command identity, not invent a new effect.
steps: Record the authoritative command receipt. || Resolve a repeated command ID to the existing result.
name: command-ack

explain: Long-lived connections must recheck sensitive resource actions as identity or permissions expire. A successful handshake does not authorize the session forever.
steps: Record initial authentication and expiry. || Deny a later action when the current time is outside that validity.
name: session-recheck

explain: A responsive connection can coexist with a stalled worker. Transport heartbeat and application progress need independent signals.
steps: Keep last pong and last task-progress times separately. || Detect a stalled task even when the connection is alive.
name: heartbeat-vs-task

explain: A new connection may reach another replica, so durable task state cannot live only on the original socket server. A shared-store abstraction provides the recoverable identity.
steps: Reconnect to a different replica. || Read the task from shared authoritative state rather than the local connection registry.
name: websocket-scale

explain: Binary media and structured control events require explicit framing and limits. Their queue policies can differ because dropping stale media is different from losing a business receipt.
steps: Classify a binary payload separately from a JSON-shaped control envelope. || Enforce media bytes and allowed control types independently.
name: binary-control

explain: A meaningful duplex test suite includes reconnect, duplicate effects, slow consumers, and permission expiry. The manifest identifies required cases and fails when evidence is absent.
steps: Declare required behavioral fixtures. || Compare them with executed case IDs rather than counting test files.
name: websocket-checks
